key_insight: A structured-judgment model and several general-purpose LLMs all achieved high accuracy for extracting smoking history from clinical notes, but they differed meaningfully in latency, cost, and performance on complex cases.
clinical_relevance: These tools can support lung cancer screening decision support by automating smoking-status, pack-year, and quit-date extraction needed to determine USPSTF and ACS eligibility.
method: Built a synthetic benchmark of 3,000 outpatient notes across template, messy, and arithmetic-heavy scenarios.
Compared TypeSafe Jev 1.13 with four LLMs using the same structured output schema.
Calculated screening eligibility from model outputs in code and measured accuracy, cost, and speed.
evidence_signal: Across 3,000 notes, all models showed high eligibility accuracy, with Jev fastest and cheapest among several models but less accurate than the strongest LLM on the most complex notes.
watch_item: Because the benchmark was synthetic and note complexity affected errors, real-world performance, integration, and safety checks should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Extracting smoking history from clinical notes for lung cancer screening decision support: comparing a structured-judgment model with general-purpose large language models
